nodes.label: std/ws* action family
nodes.rationale: Waiting on server-push streams is deliberately NOT counted as latency because it would corrupt shared percentiles; handshakes and one-shot sessions go into http_req_duration so WS percentiles stay comparable with HTTP/TCP/UDP; connection ids are per-VU and per-iteration.

nodes.label: std/db-* action family
nodes.rationale: SQL text is never interpolated — values only via params — to prevent SQL injection; prepared-statement caching is opt-in because it is incompatible with transaction-mode poolers (PgBouncer, Supabase Supavisor); identical db-connect config returns a parked id (~0ms) enabling one warm connection per VU like k6/Locust.

nodes.label: std/graphql@v1
nodes.rationale: Each document is validated against the endpoint's introspected schema before sending so a typo fails the step before any request leaves; introspection round paid once per run (process-wide cache).

nodes.label: std/grpc-* action family
nodes.rationale: No protobuf codegen: schema comes from a base64 descriptor set or server reflection (cached per URL for the run); payloads are plain JSON per protobuf-JSON mapping.

nodes.norm_label: admin console (machines, configurations, tests, runs & logs)

nodes.label: std/thresholds@v1
nodes.rationale: Thresholds read the same HDR histogram aggregates as the text summary so numbers match; a threshold on a nonexistent metric fails the run with a config error so a typo cannot silently skip the SLO; severity fail exits CLI with code 1 for CI gating.

nodes.label: pro/fix* actions
nodes.rationale: FIX data dictionary is loaded from the venue's spec (QuickFIX FIX44.xml) rather than hardcoded — only the session layer is built in, so a bare logon works schema-free; URL-form schema downloads once per process, not per session.

nodes.label: pro_llm_* metrics (ITL/TPOT percentiles, cost)
nodes.rationale: The agent ships no built-in price tables — users supply their own price list via PERFSCALE_LLM_PRICES(_FILE); a model without a matching price simply gets no cost metric, and a bad config warns once and disables cost metrics without failing the run.

nodes.label: nvidia-smi-pro GPU collector
nodes.rationale: Compute-process query runs best-effort (old drivers, WSL) — GPU rows still arrive without pro_gpu_process_* fields; per-process utilization is unavailable via nvidia-smi (needs NVML).

nodes.label: std/pubsub@v1 pro drivers (redis, mqtt, kafka)
nodes.rationale: subscribe-first ordering makes same-subject roundtrips always see their own messages; Kafka uses manual partition assignment with watermarks fixed at exchange start instead of consumer-group join because group join cannot be deterministically awaited and lazy latest-reset could miss the roundtrip's own messages; enable.auto.commit always off so a load run never moves real consumer-group offsets; unknown option keys are rejected with the supported list so a typo fails loudly.

nodes.label: Shared variables redis driver
nodes.rationale: Each operation maps to a single atomic server-side Redis command (INCRBY/RPUSH/LPOP/...) — same contract the memory driver gives with one lock acquisition — so there is no read-modify-write race and no lock primitive to hang on; each agent re-seeds keys at its own start, so state never carries between runs and pre-warmed storage cannot be relied upon until all agents connected.

nodes.label: pro/soap* actions
nodes.rationale: Raw HTTP treats 200 OK as success, a trap for SOAP since servers send Fault with both 200 and 500 — pro/soap@v1 always parses the body and fails the step on any Fault regardless of status; WSDL parser is namespace-tolerant (prefixes resolved via xmlns declarations) so nonstandard-prefix WSDLs parse correctly.

nodes.label: pro/webrtc-* actions
nodes.rationale: Engine owns the media plane (real ICE/DTLS-SRTP handshakes and RTP) while vendor-specific signaling is delegated to versioned wasm libraries so the engine does not accrete per-vendor code; only AV1 has a pure-Rust encoder (rav1e) so synthetic VP8/H.264 play a fixed 320x240 asset and true AV1 SVC is rejected with an error pointing at simulcast layers instead of silent substitution; WebRTC requires Scale/Enterprise because media-plane load is the expensive part other tools never exercise.
